steps.name: run-lock adapter and the update lock: one update at a time, a dead holder recovered
criteria: A second update while one is running refuses update.already-running as the last stderr line, reaches no service, exits 1 and leaves the running update's lock as it was
A lock left by a process that has died is recovered: update runs to the end and the lock is gone

While update runs, .cache/update.lock holds the holder's pid as decimal digits (trailing whitespace tolerated) and names a live process; the lock is removed when the run ends, after a success and after a failure, so the next run after a failed one reaches the fetch again instead of refusing
An update refused for its command line takes no lock and leaves none

The lock adapter's probe demonstrates, against the real filesystem, that the cache directory is writable and that a stale lock (a recorded pid that is not running) is detected; an unwritable .cache/ is not allowed to pass the probe silently

steps.implementation_notes: Contract shape: bounded-change; universe = the single file .cache/update.lock (created with exclusive create, removed on release); the adapter is a driven adapter injected into update.mjs as a capability (lock), never reached through a god-object. Wire, then probe, then use: harvest.mjs wires the adapter, its probe runs before any lock is taken, and a failed probe refuses to start the run with a structured refusal rather than running unlocked. Probe fault injection it must survive (feature-delta Earned Trust): a stale lock left by a killed process (liveness check on the recorded pid) and an unwritable .cache/. Taking the lock happens after the command line is parsed and before any stage (so a refused command line takes none, pinned decision 10) and releasing happens on success and on failure. Check the adapter's node:fs use against the two dependency-cruiser rules BEFORE writing it (feature-delta Technology and enforcement); if a rule needs a change, stop and report, as that is a decision. DR-0016 decision 8 and pinned decision 10 are the contract; the wording after update.already-running is not pinned. The tests use the lock helpers aLockHeldBy and aDeadPid already in support/.
